properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 11:09AM EDT until September 22 at 5:36AM EDT by NWS Northern Indiana
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne affecting
Allen IN County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Indiana...
Ohio...

Wabash River near Bluffton IN affecting Wells County.

Wabash River near Linn Grove affecting Wells and Adams Counties.

Saint Marys River near Decatur affecting Van Wert, Adams and Allen
IN Counties.

For the Wabash River...including Linn Grove, Bluffton IN, Wabash,
Logansport...Moderate flooding is forecast.
For the Saint Marys River...including Decatur, St. Mary's River near
Fort Wayne...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Saint Marys River at St. Mary's River near Fort Wayne.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Some residents in the Winchester Road area
may need to be evacuated. Property damage begins in some areas at
this level.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 12.9 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this afternoon to a crest of 16.8 feet tomorrow evening. It will
then fall below flood stage early Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Detailed river forecasts and additional information can be found at
www.weather.gov/iwx under Rivers and Lakes.

This statement will be updated within the next 12 to 24 hours.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 17 at 10:30PM MDT until September 18 at 2:15PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in central New Mexico...
West Central Chaves County in southeastern New Mexico...

* WHEN...Until 215 PM MDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flood waters in Whitetail Canyon will flow into the Rio
Felix overnight into Friday morning. Flooding of low water
crossings along the Rio Felix are expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1026 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly
in the warned area. Between 3 and 5 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are possible in the
warned area. Impacts are expected within Whitetail Canyon, along
Picacho Road, including Clements Ranch, in and along the Rio
Felix.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Southeastern Lincoln and West Central
Chaves Counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding on the Vamori Wash.

* WHERE...Southwestern Pima County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1030 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...The Vamori Wash continues to rise due to excess runoff
from earlier rainfall.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 435 AM MST, gauge reports indicate the Vamori Wash has reached
9.5 feet. At this level the Highway 21 bridge approaches flood.
If the Vamori Wash rises above 9.8 feet, Highway 21 may be
impassible. Flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly in
the warned area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Santa Cruz.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 9:18AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued September 18 at 9:08AM MDT until September 18 at 12:15PM MDT by NWS Pocatello ID
properties.description:
FFWPIH

The National Weather Service in Pocatello has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Ohio burn scar in...
Northwestern Blaine County in central Idaho...

* Until 1215 PM MDT.

* At 908 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain over the Ohio Burn Scar. The expected rainfall rate is
0.5 to 1 inch in 1 hour. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to
begin shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the Ohio burn scar. The debris flow can
consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Ohio Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Ohio Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northwestern Blaine County.
properties.instruction:
This is a life threatening situation. Heavy rainfall will cause
extensive and severe flash flooding of creeks...streams...and ditches
in the Ohio Burn Scar. Severe debris flows can also be anticipated
across roads. Roads and driveways may be washed away in places. If
you encounter flood waters...climb to safety.

CMAMtext: NWS: FLASH FLOOD WARNING this area til 12:15 PM MDT. Avoid flooded areas.
CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 12:15 PM MDT. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.
